feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong CV for a senior digital communications leader: clear positioning, credible progression, and relevant platform/strategy depth. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat repetitive, light on quantified outcomes beyond web scale, and slightly overstuffed with overlapping skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, culminating in director-level leadership and now consulting; this supports credibility and growth.  
- Strong domain alignment: digital strategy, Drupal/web modernization, analytics, governance, and multimedia are consistently reinforced across summary, experience, and skills.  
- Writing is polished and readable, with no obvious misspellings or major grammar errors; tone is professional and audience-appropriate.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable impact: include outcome metrics tied to email performance, social growth, engagement, efficiency gains, budget scope, team size, or campaign results—not just platform scale.  
- Reduce redundancy: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly. Consolidating these would improve structure and scannability.  
- Tighten style consistency: use serial commas consistently (“content operations and enterprise web improvement” → “content operations, and enterprise web improvement” only if using Oxford commas throughout), standardize hyphenation (“organization-wide,” “member-facing,” “broadcast-quality” are good), and consider “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience.”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s direction, but it is slightly generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Work Experience. It would be stronger with sharper positioning, clearer seniority, and one or two concrete differentiators.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Lead with current value proposition: senior digital strategy/communications leader for mission-driven and advocacy-focused organizations.
- Add 1–2 specific strengths reflected in recent roles, such as Drupal/web modernization, analytics infrastructure, or cross-functional governance.
- Tighten wording to reduce abstraction: replace “building the workflows and systems” with “designing governance, workflows, and digital systems.”

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social media, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, Drupal/web modernization, analytics, and digital governance. Strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear content, aligning stakeholders, and building scalable systems that improve coordination and audience engagement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflows and systems,” and “stakeholder coordination” are repeated in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. It would be stronger if it emphasized higher-value leadership capabilities rather than repeating channel and platform terms.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, senior-level language: “Enterprise digital strategy,” “CMS modernization,” “Editorial governance,” “Analytics and performance reporting,” “Cross-functional stakeholder leadership.”
- Group related items and reduce list length to 6–8 competencies for faster scanning and stronger positioning.
- Use consistent phrasing style; avoid mixing functions (“communication”) with tools/processes (“administration”).
- Possible rewrite: Enterprise digital strategy • CMS modernization & web operations • Editorial governance & workflow design • Cross-channel campaign communications • Analytics, KPI reporting & optimization • Stakeholder & cross-functional leadership • Policy, advocacy & public-sector messaging • Multimedia, livestream & event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication” and “Policy & advocacy communication” repeat the header and Topline Skills almost verbatim.
- “Web & CMS administration” and “Data analytics & reporting” are already covered more specifically in Topline Skills and Technical + IT.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good strategic/technical range, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the prior NACo positions and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level scope, distinctive contributions, and any measurable outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, web governance, campaign delivery, and AI-enabled content discovery for enterprise communications platforms.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-focused points; e.g., combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet about improving cross-channel operations.
- Emphasize consultant-specific outcomes and ownership: “Designed Drupal microsite frameworks, modular content components, and member toolkit experiences for priority campaigns.”
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/campaigns launched, publishing teams supported, traffic/user adoption, search accuracy gains, workflow time saved, or issue resolution speed.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics…” repeats themes already covered in Director of Digital Media.
- The microsite and AI search bullets overlap with Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and let projects carry the detail.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/organizational scope, and distinguish strategic leadership from the more execution-focused NACo roles before and after it.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance and budget, leading enterprise platform modernization and multi-channel communications.”
- Make bullets more outcome-led: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where missing: include team size, budget size, reporting cadence, production volume, engagement growth, cost savings, or reduced reliance on vendors for the studio build.
- Tighten phrasing: replace “including… serving thousands of followers” with a more specific result or omit follower count if it feels weak versus other metrics.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” and recurring video/programming overlap with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, modernization and infrastructure.
- Governance/workflow language also overlaps with the current consultant role; avoid repeating “governance, workflows, best practices” phrasing.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the roles before and after it. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership at this level: newsletter operations, advocacy video, and cross-team editorial systems.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, supporting NACo’s advocacy messaging and cross-channel editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-focused: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with stronger ownership and, if possible, metrics: “Built more consistent publishing workflows and editorial planning processes across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications operations across web, email, social and video” is very similar to the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this version execution-focused, not leadership/budget/governance-focused.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this entry as scaling/formalizing the program, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership

- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy

- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented, e.g., “Enterprise content strategy for high-volume, multi-publisher environments.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple NACo experience bullets; keep this section as a summary, not a repeat.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization

- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. For a topline section, emphasize highest-value, recent capabilities and group lower-level tools more cleanly.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop or de-emphasize older/lower-signal items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is still central to current work.
- Consider moving “WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages” to Technical + IT only, unless those platforms are important to target roles.
- If possible, add scope via adjacent experience instead of here, e.g., tie Drupal/CMS modernization to “10,000+ page migration” elsewhere rather than listing more tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- Platform/tool lists substantially duplicate the Technical + IT section.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value capabilities and decision-making impact over listing every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI/Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Tighten wording and group related items: “Dashboarding & leadership reporting” instead of separate “Leadership reporting.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy • KPI design • Executive dashboarding & leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity • SEO & performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current item duplicates the “Technical + IT → Data, Analytics & Optimization” section almost exactly.
- Because recent NACo experience already proves these tools, avoid repeating the full stack here unless you remove/detail-reduce the Technical + IT version.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since Drupal is central to your most recent work, this item should emphasize depth/relevance or be trimmed.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show level: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing and consistency with the rest of the CV.
- If you want more impact, replace weaker/less-used tools with evidence elsewhere rather than listing all five equally.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is largely duplicated by **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep the stronger version in one place and shorten or remove the other.
- Drupal already appears prominently in recent experience and projects, so avoid repeating it without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it feel more current and implementation-focused by emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions**
- If accurate, add scope/outcome language instead of pure tools, e.g. **Front-end development for Drupal-based sites, API-driven integrations, tag management, edge scripting, and deployment automation**
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless other skills also use version-specific naming; **HTML, CSS, JavaScript** is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Repeats **HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills; keep them in one place or make this section more tool-specific
- “GitHub Actions” and “Cloudflare Workers” are strong differentiators—prioritize these over older/basic items if space is tight

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills. Make it more purposeful by grouping tools by function and emphasizing systems you likely used most recently.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp**
- If accurate, add light functional labeling for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/workflow:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- Consider trimming older/lighter-use tools (for example Basecamp or Trello) if space is tight, so the list better supports your recent enterprise systems leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Slack/Teams are collaboration tools, not workflow systems; relabeling the category will fix that.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses a chance to signal scale or use case. Because recent roles emphasize enterprise email operations, frame these as platforms used for member communications and engagement workflows.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp** _(enterprise email campaigns, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, and member engagement workflows)_
- If accurate, add a light qualifier for strongest platform(s): **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (enterprise journeys, segmentation)** • **Higher Logic (member communications)** • **Mailchimp**
- Keep ordering by relevance/recency: put the platform most used at NACo first.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience bullets about newsletters and digital channels; avoid repeating outcomes here unless you add a distinct technical angle like segmentation, automation, or journey orchestration.
- “Engagement” also partially overlaps with “Automation & Workflow Systems”; keep this item focused on email/member communications platforms only.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs and scope if you can quantify them.

Suggested edit
- Reframe to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: size/timing of website refresh, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, email/social growth, or production cadence.
- Tighten the close: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day supervision to a digital media associate.”
- If accurate, specify tools/platforms or scale: CMS used, event coverage volume, or cross-functional partners supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; position this as the initial setup, not mature leadership.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows the start of your multimedia and innovation work, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it tighter and emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the strongest outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities.”
- Add a second sentence centered on the unique achievement: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a more specific verb/result if possible, e.g., “produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications.”
- If available, add one measurable detail: number of episodes, audience growth, internal stakeholders supported, or projects delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Podcast/multimedia work overlaps with later video and digital production roles; keep this item focused on “first podcast” and innovation/research support.
- Avoid repeating broad digital-content language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
